chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Abū Sallām, from Sowrat ibn Kuleyb, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
And on the Day of Judgment you will see those who lied against Allah—their faces will be blackened.
He عليه السلام said: One who says, "I am an Imam," while he is not an Imam.
He said: I said, "Even if he were an ʿAlawī?" He عليه السلام said: "Even if he were an ʿAlawī."
I said, "Even if he were from the descendants of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام?" He عليه السلام said: "Even if he were."

key_terms.إِمَامٌ: the divinely appointed Imam, not merely a leader by lineage or claim
key_terms.الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment, when truth and false claims are fully exposed
key_terms.عَلَوِيًّا: an ʿAlawī, one affiliated by descent to ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.كَذَبُوا: they lied; here, falsely attributing a claim of authority to Allah
key_terms.مُسْوَدَّةٌ: blackened, describing the faces of those condemned on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: Who is meant by those who lie against Allah in relation to falsely claiming the Imamate?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic warning about those who lie against Allah by applying it to one who falsely claims the Imamate. It emphasizes that rightful religious authority is determined by divine designation, not merely by lineage, even if the claimant is an ʿAlawī or from the descendants of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام.
